title: Confidentiality and release of information
subject: This guide addresses ASIC's practices regarding the disclosure of information obtained through its compulsory powers. It covers confidentiality obligations, disclosure powers, and procedural fairness requirements.
background: The guide is issued under the ASIC Law and explains ASIC's approach following the High Court decision in Johns v ASC (1993). It is intended for persons dealing with ASIC, including applicants seeking release of information and agencies such as the DPP, liquidators, and exchanges.
ruling: ASIC states it must take reasonable measures to prevent unauthorised use and disclosure of confidential information received in connection with its functions. The guide outlines ASIC's disclosure powers under sections 25, 127(4), and 127(4B), including procedures for releasing transcripts and books produced under notice or warrant. ASIC also describes how it will carry out procedural fairness obligations, giving affected persons an opportunity to be heard before releasing information. ASIC will charge costs for releasing documents or transcripts to recoup transcription, time, and copying expenses.
